MINUTES OF A SPECIAL AND REGULAR MEETING OF THE LOMITA CITY COUNCIL
  November 19, 2012

1. OPENING CEREMONIES

  a. Call Meeting to Order

A special meeting of the Lomita City Council was called to order at 6 p.m. on Monday,
November 19, 2012, in the Council Chambers, Lomita City Hall, 24300 Narbonne Avenue.

  b. Flag Salute

Mayor Gazeley led the salute to the flag.

  c. Roll Call

Those responding to roll call by Assistant City Clerk Shumway were COUNCILMEMBERS:
Estrada, Savidan, Traina, Sanchez, and Mayor Gazeley. Also present were City Manager Rock,
Assistant City Manager Sugano, City Attorney Hogin, and Assistant City Clerk Shumway.

2. ORAL COMMUNICATIONS

There were none.

CITY COUNCIL RECESSED TO CLOSED SESSION at 6:01pm

Councilmember Sanchez recused himself on item 4 of the closed session agenda due to the
fact that he resides within 500 feet of the Islamic Center of the South Bay; Councilmember
Sanchez left the room during discussion of those items.

  CLOSED SESSION

3. CONFERENCE WITH LEGAL COUNSEL – Existing Litigation
Pursuant to Government Code section 54956.9(a)
Poppin Backhoe Service v. City of Lomita

Los Angeles County Superior Court Case No. BC470129
Islamic Center of the South Bay v. City of Lomita, et al.
United States District Court LA CV12-02418

4.  CONFERENCE WITH LEGAL COUNSEL – Anticipated Litigation
Pursuant to Government Code section 54956.9(b)
Number of potential cases: 1
Letter from Steven H. Rosenbaum to City Attorney dated July 24, 2012

CITY COUNCIL RECONVENED TO OPEN SESSION at 6:21pm
  Page 1 of 5
 5.  ORAL CLOSED SESSION ANNOUNCEMENT

ADJOURN TO REGULAR MEETING
Meeting adjourned at 6:21pm

7:00 P.M. - REGULAR MEETING OF THE LOMITA CITY COUNCIL

6. OPENING CEREMONIES

  a. Call Meeting to Order

A regular meeting of the Lomita City Council was called to order at 7 p.m. on Monday,
November 19, 2012, in the Council Chambers, Lomita City Hall, 24300 Narbonne Avenue.

  b. Flag Salute

Mayor Gazeley led the salute to the flag.

  c. Invocation

Councilmember Traina gave the invocation

  d. Roll Call

Those responding to roll call by Assistant City Clerk Shumway were COUNCILMEMBERS:
Estrada, Savidan, Traina, Sanchez, and Mayor Gazeley. Also present were City Manager Rock,
Assistant City Manager Sugano, City Attorney Hogin, Community Services Director McPherron,
Public Works Director Damasse, Parks and Recreation Director Harding, Administrative
Services Director Chavez, and Assistant City Clerk Shumway.

7. APPROVAL OF AGENDA

Councilmember Estrada moved to approve the agenda. Councilmember Sanchez seconded the
motion, which carried unanimously.

City Attorney Hogin made an oral closed session announcement. City Attorney Hogin stated
that the City Council convened the regular meeting and recessed to closed session at 6:01pm
and discussed items that are listed on the posted agenda. She reported that the Council took
one reportable action. The Council unanimously approved a settlement of Poppin Backhoe
Service v. City of Lomita, the lawsuit arising out of the improvements to Lomita Park. The City
still has approximately $12,000 in unpaid purchase orders. The Council approved a settlement
agreement which provides that the City contribute $20,000, with an additional $20,000 being
contributed by the contractor Poppin’s insurance company and $30,000 being absorbed by the
Surety. City Attorney Hogin added that the amount of $20,000 will be paid from restricted park
grant funds not by the general fund of the City.

  Page 2 of 5
 8. SPECIAL PRESENTATIONS

Mayor Gazeley presented the 2012 State of the City Address. Mayor Gazeley stated that times
continue to be challenging due to the state budget crisis and the overall state of the economy.
Due to the fiscally conservative past practices of the City Council the City has been able to
maintain its 50% general fund reserve level. The general fund reserve is currently $3,937,496.
For Fiscal Year 2012-13, the City has been able to balance the general fund with the use of
carryover funds from the prior fiscal year. Mayor Gazeley added that for Fiscal Year 2013-14,
the City is cautiously optimistic that the general fund will be balanced without the use of
carryover or reserve funds. Staffing levels continue to be extremely lean, the City is currently at
45 full-time budgeted positions down from 50 full-time budgeted positions in FY 2008-09.

Mayor Gazeley continued by saying that the City Council reduced the City’s pension obligations. In
recognition of rising pension costs, the employees have agreed to contribute a higher
percentage towards their pension cost. A 2nd Tier Pension for new hires (2%@60) was
approved by the City Council and took effect in March 2012. Newly hired employees will pay
7% towards their pension. Current employees pay 3% of their salaries towards their pension.
This will save the City significant dollars in both the short and long-term.

Mayor Gazeley stated that the City welcomed a new City Manager, Michael Rock who began his
tenure on June 25, 2012. In addition, the City adopted new water rates for the next 5 years to
offset higher operational costs, water purchase costs and to fund needed water capital
improvement projects.

9. CITY MANAGER’S REPORT

None.

10. ORAL COMMUNICATIONS AND MEETING ATTENDANCE REPORTS FROM THE CITY
  COUNCIL

Councilmembers thanked Mayor Gazeley for his leadership and hard work as the City’s Mayor
in 2012. Mayor Gazeley stated that it was a great experience being Mayor and added that
during his tenure he received support from both the Council and the public.

11. ORAL COMMUNICATIONS

Joe McGrath, Lomita resident, asked City Council to consider keeping the second cross walk,
which had been previously recommended for removal. Mr. McGrath also expressed his concern
with the potential problems associated with water runoff, and how it could possibly affect
residents of Lomita.

Cindy Segawa, Lomita resident, asked if City staff could follow up on unfinished homes in the
City, as many homes have been in that state for some time and make the City looking very
unattractive.  Ms. Segawa also added that regardless of whether it is City employees
concerned about overtime issues or members of the public wish to express their issues, anyone
should be able to bring-up issues in front of the City Council and exercise their right to free
speech.

  Page 3 of 5
 Judy Daley, Representative of the Lomita Chamber of Commerce, informed those in the
attendance that the Chamber of Commerce currently has 224 members. Ms. Daley also
reminded everyone of the upcoming business mixer, which will take place at Kaiser Permanente
on November 29, 2012 from 5:30 p.m. to 7:30 p.m., as well as the Annual Holiday Toy Mixer,
which will take place at the Lomita/Harbor City Kiwanis Hall on December 5, 2012 from 5:30
p.m. to 7:30 p.m.

George Kivett, Lomita resident, complimented Mayor Gazeley on a well prepared State of the
City Address and thanked Mayor Gazeley for his service to the City as the Mayor for 2012.

12. CONSENT AGENDA

Councilmember Traina moved to approve the consent agenda.  Councilmember Estrada
seconded the motion, which carried unanimously.

  a. Motion to Waive Further Reading

  b. Recommendation to approve the minutes for the City Council Meeting held on October 15,
  2012. RECOMMEND APPROVAL.

  c. Approval of Demands

  d. Adoption of Ordinance of the City Council of the City of Lomita relating to the sale of
  alcoholic beverages – zone text amendment No. 2012-03, amending Article 56 (Sale of
  Alcoholic Beverages) Section 11-1.56.03(D)(1) of Title XI of the Lomita Municipal Code to
  replace a finding relative to crime statistics. Applicant: Miki Stein, 23701 S. Western
  Avenue, #47, Torrance, CA 90501. RECOMMEND APPROVAL.

  e. Adoption of Capital Improvement Program (FY 2012-2017)

  • Adoption of the Five Year Capital Improvement Program (CIP) for FY 2012 – 2017

  • Authorization to Solicit Proposals for the Design of the Year 1 (FY 2012-2013) Water and
  Street Improvement Projects. RECOMMEND APPROVAL

  SCHEDULED MATTERS

13. ELECTION OF MAYOR
  Election of Mayor and Mayor Pro Tem for November 2012 – November 2013.

Councilmember Savidan nominated Councilmember Estrada to be Mayor.  Councilmember
Sanchez seconded the motion, which carried unanimously.

Councilmember Sanchez nominated Councilmember Savidan to be Mayor Pro Tem.
Councilmember Gazeley seconded the motion, which carried unanimously.

14. PRESENTATION OF PLAQUE TO OUTGOING MAYOR JIM GAZELEY

  Page 4 of 5
 The Mayor’s plaque was presented to outgoing Mayor Gazeley.

ADJOURNMENT

Meeting adjourned at 7:29 p.m.

Submitted,

__________________________________
Lena Shumway, Assistant City Clerk, CMC
